sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Direct Impacts**: Extreme weather events (heatwaves, floods, storms) causing physical trauma and thermal stress.
• **Indirect Impacts**: Vector-borne diseases (Malaria, Dengue) shifting ranges due to temperature changes; water-borne diseases (Cholera) due to contamination.
• **Social Determinants**: Climate-induced migration, food insecurity (malnutrition), and mental health issues (eco-anxiety).
• **Key Metric**: The 'Lancet Countdown' on health and climate change is the gold standard for tracking global progress.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC)**: Includes the National Mission on Sustainable Habitat.
• **Heat Action Plans (HAPs)**: State-level early warning systems and public awareness campaigns to mitigate heatwave deaths.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Lack of granular health data, poor inter-departmental coordination, and inadequate climate-resilient infrastructure.
• **Solutions**: Climate-resilient health systems (WHO framework), green hospitals, and community-based surveillance.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'V-H-N-M' (Vector, Heat, Nutrition, Migration).
• **Decoded Meaning**: V (Vector-borne diseases), H (Heat-related illness), N (Nutritional insecurity), M (Migration/Mental health).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Climate Change' as solely an environmental issue. Remember it is a 'Health Emergency' as per WHO.
Mains Value Addition: Use the phrase 'Syndemic'—the synergistic interaction of climate change, malnutrition, and obesity.

keyTakeaways: Climate change is a threat multiplier for existing health vulnerabilities.
Heat Action Plans are the primary policy tool for local-level mitigation in India.
The 'One Health' framework is essential for addressing zoonotic risks exacerbated by climate change.
